spots.name: Prince's Palace of Monaco
spots.summary: The Prince's Palace of Monaco is the official residence of the Sovereign Prince of Monaco. Built in 1191 as a Genoese fortress, during its long and often dramatic history it has been bombarded and besieged by many foreign powers.

spots.name: Cathedral of Our Lady Immaculate
spots.summary: The Cathedral of Our Lady Immaculate, formerly called the Cathedral of Saint Nicholas, or informally the Cathedral of Monaco, is the Roman Catholic cathedral of the Archdiocese of Monaco in the Monaco-Ville ward of Monaco.

names.zh: 聖母無染原罪主教座堂

spots.name: Oceanographic Museum of Monaco
spots.summary: The Oceanographic Museum, is a museum of marine sciences in Monaco City, Monaco. This building is part of the Institut océanographique, which is committed to sharing its knowledge of the oceans.

spots.name: Rock of Monaco
spots.summary: The Rock of Monaco is a 62-metre (203 ft) tall monolith on the Mediterranean coast of the Principality of Monaco. It overlooks the Mediterranean Sea and the Port Hercules.

spots.name: Opéra de Monte-Carlo
spots.summary: The Opéra de Monte-Carlo is an opera house which is part of the Monte Carlo Casino located in the Principality of Monaco.

spots.name: Japanese Garden
spots.summary: The Japanese Garden is a municipal park on the Avenue Princesse Grace, in the Larvotto ward of Monaco. It is next to the Grimaldi Forum convention centre. The garden is 0.7 hectares in size, and features a stylised mountain, hill, waterfall, beach, brook, and a Zen garden for meditation.

spots.name: Sainte-Dévote Chapel

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Chapel of Sainte—Dévote is a Roman Catholic chapel dedicated to Saint Devota, the patron saint of Monaco, which lies in the Monégasque ward of Ravin de Sainte-Dévote.

spots.name: Monaco Cemetery
spots.summary: The Monaco Cemetery is a cemetery in La Colle, Principality of Monaco.

spots.name: Monaco Top Cars Collection
spots.summary: The Exhibition of HSH The Prince of Monaco's Car Collection is an automobile museum in the La Condamine district of Monaco. The museum exhibits the personal car collection of Prince Rainier III of Monaco, which he assembled of a period of thirty years.
spots.wikipediaTitle: Car Collection of Rainier III, Prince of Monaco

names.de: La Collection de S.A.S. le Prince de Monaco

spots.name: Jardin Exotique de Monaco
spots.summary: The Jardin Exotique de Monaco is a botanical garden located on a cliffside in Monaco. The garden, which first opened in 1931, primarily features exotic succulent plants.

spots.name: Napoleon Museum

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Napoleon Museum in Monte Carlo, Monaco was a museum of artifacts that once belonged to the French Emperor Napoleon I. The museum, first established in 1968, was located in the Prince of Monaco's palace. In 2014, the museum's collection was auctioned off to raise funding for renovations to the Prince's palace.

spots.name: St Martin Gardens
spots.summary: The Jardin St. Martin are located in the Monaco-Ville ward of Monaco. The gardens are made up of a series of paths on the south west face of the Rock of Monaco. They have an estimated area of 11,200 square meters.

spots.name: Avenue Princesse Grace
spots.summary: The Avenue Princesse Grace is an avenue in the Larvotto ward of Monaco. It is named after Grace Kelly, Princess consort of Monaco. It is the most expensive street in the world according to Engel & Völkers. Property along the street is on average worth $17,750 per square foot or £73,000 per square metre.

spots.name: Chapel of Mercy, Monaco-Ville

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Chapel of Mercy is a Roman Catholic church on the Rue Basse in Monaco's Monaco-Ville district.

names.fr: Chapelle de la Miséricorde de Monaco

spots.name: Statue of Juan Manuel Fangio
spots.summary: The statue of Juan Manuel Fangio is a bronze statue in Monaco, placed at Avenue du Port in the district of Monte Carlo. It was designed by Joaquim Ros i Sabaté in 1996, and unveiled at its current location on 20 May 2003.

spots.name: Stade Louis II
spots.summary: The Stade Louis II, or simply Louis II, is a stadium located in the Fontvieille district of Monaco, near the border with Cap-d'Ail commune of France. It serves primarily as a venue for Athletics and football, being the home of AS Monaco.

names.ja: スタッド・ルイ・ドゥ

spots.name: Synagogue Edmond Safra

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Synagogue Edmond Safra is an Orthodox Jewish congregation and synagogue, located at 15 avenue de la Costa, in Monte Carlo, in Monaco. The synagogue is run by the Association Cultuelle Israelite de Monaco (ACIM).

spots.name: Princess Grace Irish Library

hours.note: Closed Sun; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Princess Grace Irish Library is a library situated in Monaco named after Princess Grace, the wife and consort of Prince Rainier III.

spots.name: Museum of Stamps and Coins
spots.summary: The Museum of Stamps and Coins is located in the Fontvieille section of Monaco. It tells the postal history of the principality, and contains a display of Monegasque money dating to 1640.

names.fr: Musée des timbres et des monnaies de Monaco

spots.name: Chapelle de la Visitation, Monaco-Ville

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Museum of the Chapel of Visitation is an art museum and Roman Catholic chapel in the Monaco-Ville ward of Monaco. The baroque chapel dates from the 17th-century.

names.fr: Chapelle de la Visitation de Monaco

spots.name: Louis Notari Library

hours.note: Closed Sun; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Louis Notari Library is the National library of Monaco, founded by Prince Albert I in 1909.

spots.name: Zoological Garden of Monaco
spots.summary: The Jardin Animalier de Monaco is a zoo located on the Esplanade Rainer III, in Monaco's Fontvieille ward, on the southern side of the Rock of Monaco. It was established by Rainier III, Prince of Monaco in 1954. Almost 300 animals representing some 60 different species are held in the zoo.

photo.author: Steve Knight from Halstead, United Kingdom

spots.name: Museum of Prehistoric Anthropology

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Museum of Prehistoric Anthropology is located within the Jardin Exotique de Monaco. It was opened in 1902 and contains a collection of fossils and other excavated artifacts relating to the prehistory of Monaco and areas nearby.

names.es: Museo de Antropología Prehistórica de Mónaco

spots.name: New National Museum of Monaco
spots.summary: The New National Museum of Monaco (NMNM), formerly Musée National de Monaco, is a museum of contemporary visual art in Monaco. It is situated in two locations, the Villa Sauber and the Villa Paloma. The museum began organizing temporary exhibitions at Villa Paloma in 2010. The venues display two exhibitions annually.

spots.name: Théâtre Princesse Grace
spots.summary: The Théâtre Princesse Grace is a theatre in Monaco.

spots.name: Princess Antoinette Park
spots.summary: The Princess Antoinette Park on the Boulevard de Jardin Exotique is a municipal park in the Jardin Exotique ward of Monaco. It is named for Princess Antoinette of Monaco, the elder sister of Rainier III, Prince of Monaco. The garden is dedicated to the sacred olive tree.

spots.name: Testimonio II
spots.summary: Testimonio is a mixed-use skyscraper complex located in La Rousse, Monaco.

spots.name: Rainier III Nautical Stadium
spots.summary: The Rainier III Nautical Stadium is a municipal sports complex on the Route de la Piscine in the La Condamine district of Monaco, in Port Hercules.

spots.summary: Find all types of luxury outlets and marvel at the nice architecture of the residential buildings. To rent an apartment here can cost up to €220,000 per month.

spots.name: Grimaldi Forum
spots.summary: The Grimaldi Forum is the Monaco convention centre. Completed in 2000, the sun filled building on the sea has a remarkable glass entrance, two convention restaurants, an auditorium for ballet and opera, and two more auditoriums for meetings and other affairs. The Forum also offers two large exhibition halls that can be used for trade shows or other exhibitions. It is also a short walking distance

spots.name: Champions Promenade
spots.summary: The winner of the "Golden Foot" football player of the year award leaves a permanent mould of his footprints here.

spots.name: Monaco Yacht Show
spots.summary: Held every year in September at Port Hercules this is considered one of the biggest superyacht shows in the world with around 130 boats on display. Walk along the harbourfront on the blue carpet and marvel at yachts with a combined net worth of about US$3 billion.

spots.name: Yacht Club Monaco
spots.summary: Founded in 1953 by Prince Rainier and presided over by Prince Albert II since 1984, the Yacht Club de Monaco brings together more than 1200 members from 60 nationalities. Many of the world’s most prestigious private yachts fly the Yacht Club de Monaco’s burgee, testimony to its unique position on the international yachting scene. The new building designed by Lord Foster is in the heart of Port Her

spots.name: Monte-Carlo International Show Jumping
spots.summary: Attracts some of the best riders in the world. The course is considered very tight and challenging.

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The ultimate night club in Monaco (it's not actually in Monte Carlo), the famed Jimmy'z is frequented by royalty and the uber-rich, which isn't a surprise considering some of the hefty price tags, a beer will cost you upwards of €26. If you are not willing to afford it, there are other clubs to go to. There are two entrances: one, two floors down in Le Sporting Club, the other at street level, and

spots.name: Le Grill
spots.summary: Although often overlooked by the famed Louis XV, look above to the Hotel de Paris' rooftop for its equally elegant contender. Less intimidating than the Ducasse citadel downstairs, Le Grill offers every imaginable sort of grilled fish, and meat that come from the nearby Alps. The selection of 600,000 wines are the perfect accompaniment to every dish, and the service is impeccable. Dining on the ro

spots.name: Louis XV

hours.note: Closed Tue, Wed

spots.summary: In one of the finest hotels in the world, run by one of the finest chefs in the world (Alain Ducasse) this Michelin 3-star rated restaurant serves dining perfection among luxurious glitterati. The level of sophistication for all dishes is hard to be surpassed, the sea bass with Italian artichokes regularly reaches a score of 19/20 by restaurant critics. The restaurant contains the world's largest

spots.name: Café de Paris
spots.summary: The nerve centre of Monte Carlo, where people go to see and be seen, buzzing with the feel of old time Monte Carlo, circa early 1900s. Menu items change frequently, as do the waiters, who seem intent on rushing patrons through their meals. For people-watching, you could try a diet Coke for €6, glass of beer for €14 and ice cream for €16 (June 2017). Reservations to dine are recommended.

spots.name: The Bar @ Columbus Hotel

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: More laid-back and informal than some of its counterparts, its subdued atmosphere is a refreshing change from some of the high energy Monaco bars. Decked out in shades of blue, it's almost as sweet as the chocolate martinis, which come with a big truffle in each glass which slowly dissolves into your drinks and tastes heavenly.

spots.name: Beefbar
spots.summary: Quality cuts of beef on offer, attached with high, though surprisingly worthwhile price tag. Small cups on puree are available for the meat, though an additional cup (one is far too small), costs €8.5 (Aug 2020). Wine selections are paired perfectly with the red meat. Chic atmosphere and the staff are extremely attentive.

spots.name: Chez Roger

hours.note: Closed Sun

spots.summary: Try the typical food of the region. Socca (chickpea pancakes) for €3 and Pissaladière (caramelized onion and anchovy tart) for €2 (Aug 2020). The Monégasque speciality Barbajuan, which is a kind of fritter stuffed with spinach and other ingredients, can be bought in the shop to the right of Chez Roger's.

spots.name: Twiga

hours.note: Closed Mon

spots.summary: Showcasing panoramic views from the top floor of the Grimaldi Forum, the outdoor seating area offers the perfect spot to see yachts cruising into the harbour. Top models and the people who want to be with them dance the early mornings away. Cocktail list is impressive and bite-sized treats are available.

spots.name: Maison des pâtes Saint-Charles

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Good fresh made pasta with best Service. The pasta, gnocchi and ravioli are very good, the sauces varied and well cooked. You will only find extraordinarily delicious takeaway products here. And the welcome is always warm.

spots.name: Buddha-Bar Monte-Carlo

hours.note: Closed Mon, Sun

spots.summary: Asian bar and restaurant is quite a decadent scene and quite expensive. Expect a queue for the bar and table service with the usual club-style sparklers after 23:00.

spots.name: Cooks Monaco

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Brilliant Italian pizzas and great service. They also have a rotisserie corner with a wide choice. For real honest good food in Monaco here is the place to go.

spots.name: L'Express

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Good pizza and pasta as well as other dishes. Try the delicious "Farandole Monégasque", a sampler plate of local Monégasque dishes. Vegetarian options.

spots.name: La Rascasse

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: One of the most famous bars in the city due the final curve of the F1 track, which is named after the place.

spots.name: Mickey’s Pizza
spots.summary: Good quality pizza. Topped pizzas from €11, pizza lunch menu for €11.50 (August 2019).
